plan_a_advantages: Prioritizes climbing strength and trail-specific power.
Includes targeted threshold hill workouts for speed development.
plan_b_advantages: Longer runs provide a greater volume of trail running experience.
Incorporates strength and mobility work, which is beneficial for injury prevention and overall running mechanics.
reasoning: For a runner aiming to become faster on trails, Plan A is the superior choice. It directly addresses the need for climbing strength and trail-specific power through dedicated hill workouts, which are crucial for improving speed and efficiency on uneven terrain. Plan B, while incorporating longer runs, focuses heavily on endurance and general trail running, neglecting the specific adaptations required for faster performance. Plan A’s structured approach with repeated threshold hill sessions will build the necessary physiological adaptations more effectively than Plan B’s longer, less intense runs.
